_note: Original to Arda. Leader values are role kinds in roles.json; 'head' means the settlement's ruler, lord, reeve or elder.

kinds.label: lord's household
goals: collect every penny of the levy owed
marry the heir into a greater house
stop the townsfolk swearing a sworn commune
rebuild the old curtain wall before the next war
buy back land pawned by the last lord
goals_rural: collect the heriot owed on every death
marry the heir into a greater house
buy back land pawned by the last lord
make the villagers grind their corn at the lord's mill

kinds.label: merchant guild
goals: win a charter freeing members from road tolls
corner the {good} trade before the autumn fair
seat a guild member on the lord's council
drive foreign pedlars out of the market square
fund a new bridge and charge for crossing it

kinds.label: craft guild
names: the Hall of Hammers and Looms
goals: keep every workshop in town under the guild's rules
hold apprentice wages down and masters' fees up
win the contract to rebuild the temple roof
stop merchants bringing in cheaper foreign work

kinds.label: temple clergy
goals: raise a bell tower paid for by tithes
root out a heresy whispered in the lower streets
recover a relic lost in the last war
make the lord do public penance
found a hospice for the sick

kinds.label: shrine keepers
names: the Keepers of the Shrine of {patron}
goals: keep the old feast days alive
raise coin to re-roof the shrine
find out who has been leaving offerings at night

kinds.label: abbey
goals: extend the abbey's grazing onto the common
copy the great chronicle before it rots
win exemption from the lord's courts
shelter a fugitive who claimed sanctuary

kinds.label: town watch
goals: clear the cutpurses out of the market
win the back pay owed since the last war
keep both the lord's favour and the guilds' gifts

kinds.label: criminal gang
goals: run the smuggling of {good} through the gates
buy or break the watch captain
settle an old score with a rival crew
take a cut of every stall in the market

kinds.label: fishers' league
goals: overturn the lord's new tax on every catch
keep outsiders off the best fishing grounds
raise a chapel for the drowned

kinds.label: miners' brotherhood
names: the Brotherhood of the Deep Seam
goals: make the owners shore up the old galleries
win a fairer share of the ore price
keep the sealed gallery sealed

kinds.label: woodfolk
goals: win back the right to cut in the lord's forest
keep the wolves away from the camps
stop the new enclosures on the woodland edge

kinds.label: lightermen
goals: hold the monopoly on loading at the quays
win a rest day in the harvest season

kinds.label: commons
goals: have the old common grazing restored
see the tithe cut after a lean year
keep the young from leaving for the towns
get the lord to mend the bridge
goals_rural: have the old common grazing restored
see the tithe cut after a lean year
keep the young from leaving for the towns
get the lord to mend the bridge
stop the lord's shepherds grazing the stubble

rival: {a} and {b} have quarrelled over dues and tolls for a generation.
{a} accuse {b} of cheating them at every reckoning.
{a} and {b} will not sit at the same table at the harvest feast.
hostile: {a} and {b} have spilled blood in the alleys within the year.
A body in the millrace last spring is laid at the door of {b}, and {a} want payment.
friendly: {a} and {b} trade favours and sit together at feasts.
{a} lend money to {b}, and both like the arrangement.
allied: {a} and {b} are bound by marriages, debts and oaths.
{a} and {b} act together whenever the lord's steward comes calling.

court|merchants: {b} say the levy at the gates is robbery; {a} say {b} lie in their ledgers.
{a} have refused {b} a charter three years running.
commons|court: {a} want the old grazing rights back, and {b} have fenced the common.
Labour days owed to {b} have doubled, and {a} are muttering about a moot.
court|criminals: {b} have been bleeding the lord's tolls, and {a} have hanged two of them.
{a} want {b} gone; {b} know where the lord's debts are buried.
criminals|watch: {b} take bribes from {a} with one hand and hang them with the other.
{a} killed a watchman at the river steps last winter, and {b} have not forgotten.
criminals|temple: {b} preach against {a} from the steps every holy day.
{a} robbed the poor box of {b}, and the priests want the thieves named.
crafts|merchants: {b} import cheap foreign work and undercut {a}.
{a} say {b} fix the price of raw stuff to starve the workshops.
court|temple: {a} and {b} share the tithe and the pulpit's blessing.
{b} bless every feast of {a} and are paid for it in candles and land.
abbey|temple: {a} and {b} squabble over tithes and who may bury the dead.
court|fishers: {a} have put a tax on every catch, and {b} have stopped paying it.
{b} want the lord's weir on the river pulled down; {a} want it kept.
court|miners: {b} want the old galleries shored up; {a} want the ore faster.
{a} fined {b} for a stoppage after the last collapse.
fishers|merchants: {b} buy the catch cheap and sell it dear, and {a} know it.
{a} say {b} fix the price of salt against the boats.
court|foresters: {a} have closed the forest to cutting, and {b} cut anyway.
{b} say the lord's foresters hang men for gathering deadwood.
court|watch: {b} are paid and fed by {a}, and know which side their bread is buttered.
The captain of {b} sits at {a}'s table.
merchants|watch: {a} pay {b} a little extra to guard the warehouses.
{b} escort the caravans of {a}, for a fee.
commons|temple: {b} feed the poor of {a} in the lean months.
{a} crowd into {b}'s hall on every feast day.
abbey|commons: {a} rent their fields to {b} at fair rates.
{b} send their children to {a} to learn their letters.
abbey|court: {a} claim land that {b} say was stolen from the lord's grandfather.
criminals|merchants: {a} run protection over the stalls of {b}.
{b} hire {a} to rough up rivals, and pay late.
boatmen|criminals: {a} look the other way at night, for a share of what {b} unload.
{b} pay {a} to lose crates in the river.
boatmen|merchants: {a} and {b} split the dock dues between them.
commons|shrine: {b} keep the old feast days that {a} love.
{a} bring the first sheaf of the harvest to {b}.
merchants|miners: {a} buy ore from {b} by weight and cheat them on the scales.
{b} want to sell ore without {a} as middlemen.
